_comment: Object Investigation from Te Papa's collection. Edit, then run: TEPAPA_API_KEY=... npm run investigation. Each object becomes a puck; 'clue' is the prompt, 'hint' shows after a wrong answer, 'fact' with the reward.
title: Ngā Manu o Aotearoa
subtitle: Birds of Aotearoa, painted by J.G. Keulemans for Walter Buller's 1873 'A History of the Birds of New Zealand'

objects.name: Kākāpō
objects.clue: the world's heaviest parrot. It can't fly, it comes out at night, and males 'boom' to call for a mate.
objects.hint: Look for a big, moss-green parrot.
objects.fact: Kākāpō are critically endangered. Every living kākāpō is known by name and carefully looked after.

objects.name: Huia
objects.clue: a bird whose males and females had very different beaks: short and strong for him, long and curved for her.
objects.hint: Look for a glossy black bird with orange wattles and a white-tipped tail.
objects.fact: The huia lived only in the North Island. It has not been confirmed alive since 1907 and is now extinct.

objects.name: Tūī
objects.clue: a noisy songbird of clicks, cackles and bell-like notes, wearing a little white tuft at its throat.
objects.hint: Look for a dark bird with a white tuft under its chin.
objects.fact: Tūī drink nectar from flowers like kōwhai and harakeke, carrying pollen from plant to plant.

objects.name: Takahē
objects.clue: a large flightless bird that people thought was extinct, until it was found again in Fiordland in 1948.
objects.hint: Look for a stout blue-green bird with a big red beak.
objects.fact: Takahē are still rare, and are cared for on predator-free islands and in sanctuaries.

objects.name: Kiwi
objects.clue: a bird that sniffs out its food: it is the only bird with nostrils at the very tip of its beak.
objects.hint: Look for a round brown bird with a long, thin beak.
objects.fact: A kiwi egg is enormous for the size of the bird, up to about a fifth of the mother's weight.

objects.name: Kererū
objects.clue: a big native pigeon, and now the only bird large enough to swallow the biggest forest fruits whole and spread their seeds.
objects.hint: Look for a plump green pigeon with a white chest.
objects.fact: Kererū spread the seeds of trees like taraire, tawa and karaka, helping the forest grow.
